newsitem.title: GERMANY: Multinational board worried about Bosnian cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Multinational board worried about Bosnian cabinet.

text.p: The executive committee of the multinational contact group on Bosnia said on Tuesday it was "seriously worried" by the failure of Bosnia's ethnic groups to agree on the makeup of a council of ministers, or cabinet.

Officials of the committee, formally known as the Steering Board, on Tuesday began two days of talks near Bonn to prepare for a meeting in London on December 4 and 5 of the foreign ministers of the Peace Implementation Council (PIC), overseeing the year-old Bosnian peace settlement.

"The Steering Board urged the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina to establish a joint council of ministers without delay, so that Bosnia and Herzegovina will be properly represented at the forthcoming meeting of the PIC," Germany's Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
The Moslem, Serb and Croat leaders in Bosnia's new presidency have so far failed to agree on the size and powers of their first postwar government.

The council, expected to include at least a prime minister, foreign minister and foreign trade minister, is supposed to preside over a union of autonomous Moslem-Croat and Serb entities enshrined in the 1995 Dayton peace agreement.

The Steering Board also said it condemned a protest outside the office of international mediator Carl Bildt in Sarajevo on Tuesday by angry women accusing the international community of failing to honour promises made in the Dayton accord.
The crowd jostled Bildt's deputy Michael Steiner as he left the building and pummelled his car with their fists.
"The Steering Board urges the authorities in Bosnia to guarantee the security of the High Representative (Bildt) and his staff," it said in a statement.
